TRADITIONAL AND COMPLEMENTARY MEDICINE ACT 2016

TRADITIONAL AND COMPLEMENTARY MEDICINE (AMENDMENT) REGULATIONS 2025

IN exercise of the powers conferred by paragraphs 60(2)(b), (c), (d), (e), (k)

and (m) of the Traditional and Complementary Medicine Act 2016 [Act 775], the Minister

makes the following regulations:

Citation and commencement

1. (1) These regulations may be cited as the Traditional and Complementary

Medicine (Amendment) Regulations 2025.

(2) These Regulations come into operation on 1 September 2025.

Amendment of regulation 2

2. The Traditional and Complementary Medicine Regulations 2021

[P.U. (A) 69/2021], which are referred to as the "principal Regulations" in these

Regulations, are amended in subregulation (2)—

(a) in paragraph (b), by substituting for the words "; or" at the end of the

paragraph a full stop; and

(b) by deleting paragraph (c).

Amendment of regulation 4

3. Regulation 4 of the principal Regulations is amended—

(a) by substituting for subregulation (2) the following subregulation:

"(2) An applicant referred to in subregulation (1) shall be eligible

to be registered with the Council if the applicant obtains the recognized

qualification as specified in the Third Schedule."; and

(b) in subregulation (4), by substituting for paragraph (c) the following

paragraph:

"(c) a certified true copy of a degree, diploma or certificate, or if such

degree, diploma or certificate is yet to be issued, a certified true

copy of a transcript of such degree, diploma or certificate.".

New regulation 5A

4. The principal Regulations are amended by inserting after regulation 5

the following regulation:

"Application for amendment of details in temporary practising certificate

5A. (1) Any holder of a temporary practising certificate may make an

application in writing to the Council in the form as determined by the Council

to amend any details in the temporary practising certificate and such application

shall be accompanied by the payment of fee as specified in the Second Schedule.

(2) The Council shall, after the application made under

subregulation (1) is approved, issue a new temporary practising certificate in

Form H of the First Schedule and cancel the temporary practising certificate

issued previously under subregulation 5(3).".

New regulation 6A

5. The principal Regulations are amended by inserting after regulation 6

the following regulation:

"Application for amendment of details in registered practitioner's practising

certificate

6A. (1) Any registered practitioner may make an application in writing to

the Council in the form as determined by the Council to amend any details in the

registered practitioner's practising certificate and such application shall be

accompanied by the payment of fee as specified in the Second Schedule.

(2) The Council shall, after the application made under

subregulation (1) is approved, issue a new registered practitioner's practising

certificate in Form K of the First Schedule and cancel the registered practitioner's

practising certificate issued previously under subregulation 6(4).".

New regulation 10A

6. The principal Regulations are amended by inserting after regulation 10

the following regulation:

"Application for certificate of good standing

10A. (1) Any registered practitioner who has been granted by the Council

a registered practitioner's practising certificate or a temporary practising

certificate may make an application to the Council in writing in the form

as determined by the Council for a certificate of good standing.

(2) The application made under subregulation (1) shall be accompanied

by the payment of fee as specified in the Second Schedule and subject to any

condition as determined by the Council.".

Substitution of Second Schedule

the following schedule:

[Subregulations 2(1), 4(1), 5(1), 5A(1), 6(1), 6(3), 6A(1), 7(1),

1. A subarea refers to the breakdown of traditional Malay medicine based on

treatment methods.

2. A subfield refers to the breakdown of traditional Indian medicine based on

different practices.

3. A diploma or equivalent refers to a diploma as approved or recognized by the

Traditional and Complementary Medicine Council and as specified in the

registration guidelines for the respective recognized practice area.

4. A bachelor degree or equivalent refers to a bachelor degree as approved or

recognized by the Traditional and Complementary Medicine Council and as

specified in the registration guidelines for the respective recognized practice

area.".

Deletion of Fourth Schedule

9. The principal Regulations are amended by deleting the Fourth Schedule.
